issues.issue_description: Condition: Fuses or breakers too big. A qualified electrician should further evaluate the breaker size compared to the gauge of wire. For example, there is a 40-amp breaker powering a 10-gauge wire. This breaker is also "double-tapped" with an 8-gauge stranded wire, which is generally not permitted. Implication(s): Equipment overheating | Fire hazard. Task: Further evaluation. Time: Immediate.
issues.issue_summary: An electrical panel has an oversized 40-amp breaker on a 10-gauge wire and an improper 'double-tap'. This is a fire hazard and requires immediate evaluation by a qualified electrician.

issues.issue_name: Inoperative Gas Fireplace with Incomplete Venting
issues.issue_description: Condition: Inoperative. The exhaust vent installation for the gas fireplace is incomplete, which will allow hazardous combustion gases into the home if used. This can be a life safety issue. A technician needs to evaluate the installation compared to the manufacturer's installation requirements and make corrections before the fireplace can be safely used. Task: Correct. Time: Before use.
issues.issue_summary: The basement gas fireplace is inoperative due to an incomplete exhaust vent, which poses a life safety risk from combustion gases. It must be corrected by a qualified technician before use.

issues.issue_description: Condition: Amount less than current standards. The attic insulation is lower than current standards. Increasing insulation is considered a discretionary improvement that may improve comfort and lower energy bills. Check eligibility for home efficiency rebates. Implication: Increased heating and cooling costs. Location: Attic. Task: Improve. Time: Discretionary.
issues.issue_summary: The attic insulation (R-20) is below current standards, which can lead to higher energy costs. Improving the insulation is a discretionary upgrade that could improve comfort and efficiency.

issues.issue_description: Condition: Nonstandard shape or material. Residential traps should be P-type. The current waste plumbing installation (including the dishwasher connection downstream of the trap) should be evaluated by a qualified plumber and corrected. Monitor for odors that may indicate siphoning allowing sewer gases to enter the home. Implication(s): Reduced operability | Fixtures slow to drain. Location: Kitchen. Task: Correct. Time: As soon as reasonably practical.
issues.issue_summary: The kitchen sink has a non-standard plumbing trap (likely an S-trap) which can cause slow draining and allow sewer gas to enter. It should be evaluated and corrected by a qualified plumber.
